question: Does the within-project-year release timing modify how capture condition ranks migration initiation, beyond an additive silvering-stage/body-condition model, in out-of-project predictions?
training: 6-fold leave-one-entire-project-out: fit independent coefficients in five projects using fixed expert-corrected activation; 575 heldout fish total; no heldout outcomes used to train either score.
base_predictors: project-year fixed intercept, centered length per 100 mm, centered release time per 100 days, ordinal Durif score, allometric weight-for-length condition centered within project-year
interaction_predictors: base predictors plus centered condition times centered release time per 100 days
primary_metric: paired difference in pooled within-project-year initiator/non-initiator concordance AUC (interaction minus additive); evaluate held-out projects only; source release date, not downstream event date.
secondary_metrics: per-heldout-project AUC change and pair count
6 independent-project bootstrap CI with 10000 resamples of project summaries
within-project-year early/late AUC where each half has both initiators and noninitiators; descriptive only
inference_rule: An improved portable seasonal condition gate requires positive heldout pooled AUC delta and six-project bootstrap CI fully greater than zero with no strong project reversals. Otherwise classify not supported as a general mechanism; an individual project gain does not establish hydrological cues.
outcome_guardrails: No source-outcome or event-time information for predictor transforms; center condition and release time using only heldout-project predictor values without outcomes (transductive).
Do not infer discharge, tidal windows, temperature, energy storage, or lunar effects from release-date timing.
Release date may be tagging/sampling design, not true environmental opportunity. A direct seasonal hydrology mechanism requires matched environmental data.
Do not select interaction functional form or favorable project after seeing results.
Project bootstrap has n=6 clusters, frozen training coefficients, and only reports conditional resampling uncertainty; cannot make causal claims.
Keep published V4 findings unchanged unless the new result itself warrants an explicitly post-hoc supplement.
